references.title: librosa chroma features
references.text: Chroma summarizes energy across twelve pitch classes. It is a harmonic and pitch-pattern proxy, not a transcription of melody or proof that tunes are identical.

references.title: librosa spectral centroid
references.text: The spectral centroid is the weighted mean frequency of a spectrum. Spectral statistics and MFCCs summarize sound color or timbre but cannot establish an instrument identity.

references.title: MERT research paper
references.text: MERT is a pretrained music representation encoder. Frozen embeddings can support downstream tasks, but cosine similarity is not a calibrated probability of musical similarity or an instrument prediction.

references.title: librosa beat tracking
references.text: Tempo estimates describe beat rate in beats per minute. Onset strength and beat tracking estimate periodic activity; half-time and double-time ambiguities can occur. Tempo alone does not determine rhythmic similarity.

references.title: librosa dynamic time warping
references.text: Dynamic time warping aligns ordered feature sequences with different timing. Chroma alignment can compare harmonic progressions while allowing time stretching. It does not identify copying.

references.title: AST AudioSet model and official preprocessing
references.text: Audio Spectrogram Transformer predicts AudioSet sound-event classes from log-Mel features at 16 kHz. Musical-instrument class scores are model outputs, not verified identities, calibrated similarity probabilities or absence proofs. Predictions only describe analyzed excerpts; reliability on these recordings requires instrument annotations.

references.title: EnCodec: High Fidelity Neural Audio Compression
references.text: EnCodec encodes waveforms into residual vector-quantized audio codes for reconstruction. Token distributions can be compared as exploratory texture descriptors. Tokens do not directly identify instruments, production techniques or vocal delivery; human similarity requires separate validation.
